newsitem.title: GERMANY: Toepfer sees slight fall in 1997 EU feed imports.
newsitem.headline: Toepfer sees slight fall in 1997 EU feed imports.

text.p: Animal feeds imports in the European Union should be slightly lower than the 37-37.5 million estimated for 1996, German trader Alfred C Toepfer said in a monthly market report issued on Friday.
Stressing the 1996 figure was an estimate, Toepfer said it was down two million tonnes from 1995 and around six million tonnes below the 1994 figure which reflected a bad grain crop.
An increase in grains feeding has negatively effected imported starch feeds, especially those of tapioca, and the use of protein feeds had also dropped in 1996, Toepfer said.
The trend should continue this year because another huge EU grain crop was on the cards.
EU land set-aside was lower and the crop in the ground was developing quite well and could amount to 210 million tonnes after 201-205 million estimated for 1996 by a range of sources.
East Asian protein feeds demand was boosting global prices and this should also reduce the demand fo oil meals in the EU.
Total grains use in feeds in the EU in 1996/97 (July/June) could rise to 107 million tonnes from 102 million in 1995/96, Toepfer said, adding wheat would be most affected.
EU compound feed output in 96/97 was seen stagnant at the 95/96 figure of 121 million tonnes.
Beef cattle and dairy cow feed output should fall in line with livestock reductions in the wake of the mad cow crisis, which discouraged consumption.
Pigfeed output should decline slightly but that of poultry feed should increase, both in line with consumption patterns.
The share of grain in EU mixed feeds averaged 44 percent in 95/96 and could rise to 46 percent in 96/97, Toepfer estimated.

It cited a higher intrinsic grains share in pig and poultry feed, demand for which is set to expand, as well as prospects of higher compound feed production in Spain and Italy which traditionally use a high proportion of grain. -Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
